title: Setting Clear Construction Business Goals
meta_description: How to set construction business goals that hold: start with a vision the team understands, make them SMART, and choose growth the business can sustain.
hero_subtitle: A practical guide to goals your team can actually act on.

intro.answer: A goal nobody can measure is a wish. Setting clear construction business goals is not only about profit, it is about giving everyone in the company the same idea of what a good year looks like.

image.alt: A construction business owner setting goals for the year ahead

intro.roadmap: This guide covers starting from a vision and a mission statement, turning that into SMART goals, choosing growth the business can sustain, and the areas worth aiming at: client satisfaction, your team, and digital capability.

briefing.title: Start With the Vision, Not the Number
briefing.intro: Most goal setting starts with a turnover figure and works backwards, which is why so much of it is abandoned by March. The businesses that hold their goals start somewhere less obvious: what the company is actually for, written plainly enough that the team can repeat it.

panels.heading: How do you set construction business goals that stick?
paragraphs: Start by defining the company's vision, and write a mission statement that captures it. Keep it concise, easy to understand and memorable, because its job is to guide decisions when you are not in the room.
Then make each goal SMART: specific, measurable, achievable, realistic and timely. A goal that fails any one of those five will quietly stop being mentioned.

panels.heading: Then choose growth you can sustain
paragraphs: Growth that outruns the team or the cash is not growth, it is exposure. These are the directions worth considering.
steps: Expand into new markets, where you already have a right to win.
Offer new services that your existing clients are already buying elsewhere.
Invest in your team, because capacity is usually the real ceiling.
Focus on client satisfaction, which is the cheapest source of the next job.
Build digital capability rather than adding tools.

review.label: The test
review.text: Ask three people in the business what this year's goals are. If you get three different answers, the goals exist on paper but not in the company.
